source.episode_title: Even So Must the Son of Man Be Lifted Up
source.anchor_kjv: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
source.thread: The same lifting that shamed Him is the word John later uses for His glory.
source.hook_line: By night, Jesus tells a Pharisee something strange: this defeat is what John calls His glory.
source.spoken_script: By night, Jesus tells a Pharisee something strange: this defeat is what John calls His glory. Jesus means it literally: what shames Him is what glorifies Him. Centuries earlier, a bronze serpent healed dying Israel with a look. Jesus tells Nicodemus, 'And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.' A skeptic hears cruelty. John uses that word again at the cross: shame and glory, one lifting. That word will not let you split them. You cannot want Christ's glory without His cross. He was shamed to become your glory. Believe on Christ, lifted up for you, and live.

platforms.label: YouTube (Short)
platforms.title: One Word Joins Jesus' Shame and His Glory
platforms.description:
By night, Jesus tells a Pharisee something strange: the lifting that shames Him is what John calls His glory.

"And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life." (John 3:14-15, KJV)

Centuries earlier a bronze serpent healed dying Israel with a look. John uses the same word of lifting again at the cross: shame and glory, one lifting. You cannot want Christ's glory without His cross.

Believe on Christ, lifted up for you, and live.
